_README: SHARED CROSS-REPOSITORY WIRE FIXTURE - Electronic Clapboard over CAN3.
OWNERSHIP: the Jugglebot repo OWNS this file, at
tests/fixtures/clapboard_wire_vectors.json. The Electronic-Clapboard repo
VENDORS a byte-identical copy and pins it with a checksum test. Jugglebot
has the stricter gate (run_tests.sh --full runs on every commit), so it
holds the artefact. Owner decision, 2026-08-16, recorded in
plans/active/clapboard-can3-integration.md section 6.
WHAT THE CLAPBOARD REPO MUST DO:
1. Copy this file verbatim into its own tree. Pick a path its build
system is happy with - PlatformIO treats every directory under test/
as a test suite, so a bare test/fixtures/ may not be the right home;
that choice is the clapboard repo's, not Jugglebot's.
2. Copy the published SHA-256 from clapboard_wire_vectors.json.sha256
beside it and assert, in its own test suite, that the vendored copy
still hashes to that value. That test is what makes a silent
divergence impossible.
3. Assert its can_frames.h encoders/decoders reproduce every vector
here, exactly as tests/ros/test_clapboard_wire_vectors.py does on
the Jugglebot side.
4. Re-vendor (and re-pin the hash) whenever Jugglebot publishes a new
one. NEITHER SIDE MAY CHANGE A VECTOR UNILATERALLY - a change here
is a change to docs/protocol.md section 8, which is normative and
jointly owned.
WHY THE VECTORS EXIST: docs/protocol.md section 8 documents the byte
layouts but is silent on four rules that only code enforces. They are
listed under unstated_rules below, and each has a vector that fails if
either side forgets it.
DERIVATION: every byte here was built from docs/protocol.md section 8 and
src/can_frames.h, NOT from the Jugglebot encoders - so the agreement test
is a second opinion rather than a snapshot. Vectors whose name begins
'peer/' are carried across from that repo's own test assertions verbatim,
so the two suites agree by construction. The recipe is committed at
tools/probes/clapboard_wire_vectors_gen.py; do not hand-edit this file.
normative_spec: Electronic-Clapboard docs/protocol.md section 8 (jointly owned; neither side may change it unilaterally)

unstated_rules.rule: EVERY frame in this contract, both directions, is exactly DLC 8. A receiver drops any other length silently - no error on either side.

CLAP_FIRE_EVENT bytes 0-5 are the LOW 48 BITS of a Unix-epoch microsecond clock that needs 51. The receiver must reconstruct the high bits from its own clock; taking the field at face value stamps every flash in 1978.
unstated_rules.protocol_md_says: 8.8's '~8.9 years' is the WRAP PERIOD, not the representable range, and no reconstruction rule is given.

unstated_rules.rule: All CHUNKS_PER_FIELD (5) chunks are sent for every PRESENT field, even a 1-byte value. Follows from combining 8.4's patch semantics (panel field buffers persist between transactions) with a CRC over the full 32-byte padded buffer: a prefix-only send leaves the previous value's tail in the receiver, rendering wrong text AND producing a spurious CRC_MISMATCH.
unstated_rules.enforced_in: ros_ws/src/jugglebot/jugglebot/clapboard_slate.py (build_transaction; sender-side, because the clapboard cannot detect the difference except as a CRC failure)

unstated_rules.rule: A commit naming NO field (a repaint) CRCs to the init value 0xFFFF. Both sides must agree or every repaint-only commit is rejected.
unstated_rules.enforced_in: Electronic-Clapboard src/can_frames.h:170-184 (the loop body is skipped for every absent field)
unstated_rules.pinned_by: tests/ros/test_clapboard_wire_vectors.py (the empty-present-set CRC vector + the repaint-only transaction)

known_answers.name: canonical-check-value
known_answers.note: The canonical CCITT-FALSE check value. If this fails the two repos have DIFFERENT CRC variants and every commit is rejected on the wire.

known_answers.name: empty-input
known_answers.note: Empty input returns the init value untouched - which is also why a repaint-only commit CRCs to 0xFFFF.

crc16_over_fields.name: peer/order-independent-set
crc16_over_fields.note: Fields 0-3 of the peer's order-independence case. The peer asserts only that two fill orders agree; the literal value is derived here so both repos pin the same number.

crc16_over_fields.name: peer/single-field-scene
crc16_over_fields.note: A stale buffer in an ABSENT field must not change this value - patch semantics make stale buffers the normal case, not an edge case.

crc16_over_fields.name: peer/stale-field-now-present
crc16_over_fields.note: Same buffers as peer/single-field-scene with field 3 now IN the mask. Must differ from it, or the mask is not being honoured.

crc16_over_fields.name: peer/bit-flip-good
crc16_over_fields.note: Pairs with peer/bit-flip-corrupted: one flipped bit inside the text must change the CRC.

crc16_over_fields.name: peer/bit-flip-corrupted
crc16_over_fields.note: peer/bit-flip-good with byte 3 of the text XORed by 0x01.

crc16_over_fields.name: empty-present-set
crc16_over_fields.note: UNSTATED RULE: a repaint-only commit names no field, so the CRC is the untouched init value. protocol.md 8.4 does not say so; it follows from crc16_over_fields skipping every absent field.

frames.name: peer/field-chunk-f5-seq3-abcdefg
frames.note: The peer's own layout golden, carried across EXACTLY: field 5 / seq 3 -> d[0] == 0x35, d[1] == 'a', d[7] == 'g'. buffer32 is the 32-byte field buffer whose seq-3 chunk reproduces it.

frames.name: field-chunk-f0-seq0-empty-field
frames.note: Clearing a field is a present field with an all-NUL buffer, not an absent one. Still five chunks, still DLC 8.

frames.name: field-chunk-f7-seq4-boundary
frames.note: Both nibbles at their limit (field 7, seq 4 -> d[0] == 0x47), and the last chunk of a MAXIMUM-length field: 4 text bytes then the 3 trailing NULs that let the receiver find the terminator.

frames.name: peer/commit-t3-mask0b1011-txn200-crcBEEF
frames.note: The peer's own layout golden, carried across EXACTLY: template 3 / mask 0b00001011 / flags 0x01 / txn 200 / crc 0xBEEF -> d[4] == 0xEF, d[5] == 0xBE (little-endian), d[6..7] == 0 (reserved, must be 0).

frames.name: link-ros2-up
frames.note: THE named first-integration-bug guard. Byte 0 is the only meaningful byte, so a 1-byte frame is the natural implementation - and the clapboard drops any DLC != 8 silently, leaving the panel in screensaver forever with no error on either side.

frames.name: link-ros2-down
frames.note: Screensaver is the safe default, so every link state short of UP reports DOWN. DLC 8 in this direction too.

frames.name: peer/link-any-nonzero-is-up
frames.note: The bridge never emits this, but the clapboard MUST read it as UP: a strict ==1 would turn a future flag bit in byte 0 into a silent permanent 'ROS2 down', which fails in the direction that blanks the panel. Recorded so a future bridge-side flag bit is safe by construction.

frames.name: peer/ack-txn42-crc-mismatch-2500ms
frames.note: The peer's own layout golden, carried across EXACTLY: txn 42, outcome CRC_MISMATCH (0x02), state IDLE (0x01), render_ms 2500 = 0x09C4 little-endian at bytes 3-4, bytes 5-7 reserved and zeroed.

frames.name: ack-txn1-ok-1800ms
frames.note: The happy path a SetSlate goal ends on: OK, still RENDERING at ack time, render_ms inside the 1500-3500 ms full-refresh envelope.

frames.name: peer/heartbeat-screensaver-wifi-timesynced
frames.note: The peer's own layout golden, carried across EXACTLY: state SCREENSAVER (3), flags bit2|bit4 == 0x14, fires 0x0102 little-endian at bytes 2-3, rail_mv 0 (no divider fitted), template 2, last_error 3.

frames.name: heartbeat-idle-all-flags
frames.note: Every flag set, a real rail reading (3299 mV), no errors yet. time_synced is the load-bearing one: while it is false the clapboard emits NO fire events at all, so a gap between fires_since_boot and published events is expected, not a defect.

frames.name: peer/fire-event-48bit
frames.note: The peer's own layout golden, carried across EXACTLY: 48-bit little-endian microseconds in bytes 0-5, fires_since_boot in 6-7.

frames.name: peer/fire-event-overflow-does-not-corrupt-seq
frames.note: The peer's own golden for the mask: a wall clock above 2^48 is truncated and must NOT bleed into bytes 6-7. This is the frame that makes the UNSTATED 48-bit rule visible - see unstated_rules.

frames.name: peer/time-sync-1786000000s-999999us
frames.note: Not a clapboard-block id, but the bridge emits it on this same bus and the clapboard's decoder requires DLC 8 for it too - so it is in scope for the DLC-8 emission invariant. pack('<II', sec, usec), matching broadcast_0x7dd(). usec >= 1e6 is REJECTED by the peer rather than folded in: a wrong anchor is worse than no anchor.

transactions.name: full-slate-8-fields
transactions.note: The worst case: 8 present fields x 5 chunks + 1 commit = 41 frames, the number CLAP_MAX_FRAMES (48) is sized from. Field 3 is present and EMPTY (a clear), field 5 is exactly 32 bytes. Commit is LAST.

transactions.name: single-field-patch
transactions.note: UNSTATED RULE: all five chunks go out even for a 7-byte value. Panel field buffers persist between transactions (8.4 patch semantics) and the CRC covers the full 32-byte buffer, so a prefix-only send leaves the previous value's tail in the receiver -> wrong text AND a spurious CRC_MISMATCH.

transactions.name: repaint-only-no-fields
transactions.note: A commit with an empty mask: repaint what is already there. One frame, CRC 0xFFFF, force-full-refresh flag set.
